handled_verified.description: Node types the analyzer reads and emits from, each pinned by a fixture in validation/m14/fixtures/nim/ (5 pass, every fixture source accepted by the Nim 2.2.12 compiler), by the 15-check index seam in script/m14/verify-nim-pipeline-e2e.ts, or by the NIM differential lane in script/m14/differential.ts (nim@60 941/941 covered, MISSING=0, unexplained=0%; pixie@60 3220/3220, MISSING=0, unexplained=0%). The declaration types are the whole surface: proc/func/method/iterator/template/macro/converter _declaration, type_declaration, variable_declaration with its const/let/var/using _section, object_declaration, enum_declaration, concept_declaration, and field_declaration / enum_field_declaration / variant_discriminator_declaration members; the call types are call and dot_generic_call; the rest are the name-, path- and argument-bearing payload nodes reached through grammar FIELDS (name, body, pragmas, module, operator, left, right, function, first_argument, type, items, source) or through node types. M14 NIM wave: no node type is matched by a source-text prefix (the analyzer contains no RegExp at all), and no field is read that the pinned grammar does not declare. Two families were found by the differential rather than by inspection and are the reason this list is evidence-backed rather than asserted: a destructuring binding (tuple_deconstruct_declaration wrapping symbol_declaration) never entered its scope frame, so a read was misattributed to a same-named struct property; and a path deeper than two segments was dropped whole because the grammar models the separator as a named `operator` node whose text is the entire token.

internal_silent.description: Container, literal, comment and payload nodes that correctly emit no symbol and no relationship: they are reached by the walk and carry nothing the taxonomy has a row for. Three of these deserve the reason spelled out, because "unreferenced" is not the same as "ignored": (1) field_declaration_list and variant_declaration — a `case` block's fields are field_declaration INSIDE the variant_declaration, and the field rule emits them, so the container itself is silent while its members are handled (verified: a variant object emits properties isCircle, radius, side, name, plainField); (2) pragma_expression — a pragma wrapped around an expression contributes only its arguments, and the declaration-level pragmas are read from the `pragmas` FIELD, so this node type is a second route to the same names rather than a missing one; (3) an anonymous tuple VALUE has no name to resolve, so there is nothing for `instantiates` to point at (a NAMED construction, `TypeName(field: v)`, is handled and is the shape the corpus exercises 93 times). The `tuple_construction` NODE TYPE itself moved OUT of this bucket: in a type RHS it is the ordinary spelling of an unnamed tuple type (`type T = (int, string)`, which the compiler accepts with 0 errors), and the classifier reads it. It was misfiled here until the mutation run proved the rule behind the filing was false. The literal set (integer/float/char/nil/custom_numeric/generalized_string and their content and escape payloads) emits nothing by contract: a literal value is not a declaration and its text is not a name. The bare-statement set (assembly, bind, discard, mixin, raise, return, static, yield) declares nothing; `return`/`raise`/`yield` carry no reference the analyzer would invent a target for.

gap.description: No confirmed analyzer gap: every one of the 127 named types the pinned wasm declares is either handled or a silent container, and the differential reports MISSING=0 and unexplained=0 in both directions on both corpora. The mutation gate is the second line of defence and it is what found the last two defects: 40 mutants (one per symbol kind, per relationship kind, per ruled rule, and per payload row), 27 caught on the first run, and the 13 survivors were suite holes rather than weak mutants. Chasing them found that a tuple type was never published as a struct in EITHER of the two ways Nim spells one — the grammar wraps a type RHS in `type_expression` and the classifier read the wrapper — and that an unnamed tuple element published properties named after builtin types. Both are fixed and both are now pinned in both directions, so a half-fix fails: 40/40 caught. The OPEN work in this lane is a GRAMMAR gap, which is a different ledger: 11 named node types are never reached because the pinned grammar cannot parse the construct that would produce them (do-pragma is consumed as a block comment, so no pragma node appears; a multi-line leading-dot chain, nested bracket generics `f[A, seq[B]]`, a single-line `if cond: stmt`, a `$` inside a string literal, a command-style call with a multi-line argument, a qualified type in a declaration, a pragma on a generic parameter, `func(…)` as a type, an empty tuple `(;)`, and a bare-identifier tuple construction). Those are recorded in docs/analyzers/real-nim-analyzer.md with their site counts and named classes, and a 56-line do-pragma patch is preserved unapplied at $HOME/fixtures/nim/out/0001-nim-dopragma.patch because a rebuilt wasm has not yet passed the 72-case conformance suite, the 17-file compiler matrix and the corpus regression.

design_decision.description: Owner rulings. Each is a deliberate refusal to publish, not a silence.

decisions.question: A file-scope pragma statement (`{.push checks: off.}`, `{.warning: nil.}`) names pragmas that the analyzer does not publish anywhere. Should it?
decisions.resolution: No, and the reason is that the taxonomy has no row for a file-scope decorator: the symbols row is per declaration, and a pragma statement is not a declaration. The pragma NAMES that matter are already published — as `decorators` on each declaration that carries its own `pragmas` field, which is where they have an effect. Publishing the file-scope statement as well would produce a row whose target is a name no symbol declares, i.e. a dangling edge on purpose. Left RULED rather than silent so that the absence is a decision on the record.

decisions.question: An `overrides` edge needs the project-wide type hierarchy. The analyzer is per-file. Resolve against a corpus-wide name set?
decisions.resolution: No. A same-named method on an unrelated type is a collision, and emitting the edge would assert an inheritance relation the source never states. `overrides` is emitted only when the base is declared in the same file, which is what the fixture, the seam and the targeted 71-file method-heavy draw exercise (40 overrides, matching on both sides). The cross-file case is a declared limit of a per-file analyzer, not a gap to be papered over with a wider name set.

decisions.question: Nim has `concept`, which looks like an interface, and the base ontology has an `implements` relationship. Does a concept satisfaction emit it?
decisions.resolution: No. A concept is satisfied by implicit structural dispatch, and Nim has no nominal subtype declaration to point at, so there is no name in the file that says "X implements Y" — the fact is computed by the compiler from the method set. A concept DECLARATION is emitted as a SymbolKind.Interface symbol (it is the structural contract), but no relationship is invented for satisfaction. The differential reports the label vacuous (0 truth, 0 analyzer) rather than pretending it is covered.

decisions.question: The grammar's own file-types declares `nimble`, and 171 tracked .nimble files exist in the corpus. Route them to the nim analyzer?
decisions.resolution: YES, on measurement rather than on the grammar's file-types list — declaring a format is not evidence the analyzer models it, and routing on the declaration alone is the claim-without-coverage class. Measured over every tracked .nimble of all 12 pinned corpora: 171 files, 0 error files, 0 error nodes, 26 symbols, 315 relationships, 11 imports. 100% parse health, and a .nimble's `task`/`bin` blocks declare real things rather than being pure data, so it belongs in the symbol graph. The corpus parse record already covered these files (5,227 total, of which 5,056 are .nim/.nims); the complexity artifact measured the .nim/.nims subset and recorded the 171 .nimble share separately, so neither record silently claims the other's coverage.

decisions.question: `.nims` is a Nim configuration script, in the grammar's file-types and 65 tracked files in the corpus. Route it?
decisions.resolution: YES, and on the same measurement: 65 files, 0 error files, 0 error nodes, 43 symbols, 279 relationships, 96 imports. A .nims is NimScript — set_cmd, switch, buildFile, all procs and calls on a real stdlib — so it is Nim code by any reading that matters, and the analyzer extracts it like any other module. `src/ast/language-detection.ts` now routes .nims and .nimble to nim, and the differential and fixture lanes' ext lists were updated in the same change so the claim and the router cannot drift apart: a lane that swept an extension the router skips is the inert-pin class, and a lane that under-reports what the router now handles is the same defect wearing a hat.
